statement: A rectangular garden has a perimeter of $86$ feet. The length of the garden is $7$ feet more than its width. What is the width of the garden, in feet?

choices.misconception: I doubled the width terms but added the $7$ only once, writing $4w + 7 = 86$, so I got $w = 19.75$.
I solved for the width correctly, $18$ feet, but then gave the length, $18 + 7 = 25$ feet.
I added one width and one length, $w + (w + 7) = 86$, forgetting that a perimeter goes around all four sides, so I got $39.5$.

hints: Write the length in terms of the width.
If the width is $w$, the length is $w + 7$. The perimeter adds two widths and two lengths.

solutions.reliable: Let the width be $w$ feet, so the length is $w + 7$ feet. The perimeter is $2w + 2(w + 7) = 4w + 14$, so $4w + 14 = 86$, $4w = 72$ and $w = 18$. Check: the garden is $18$ by $25$ feet, and $2(18) + 2(25) = 36 + 50 = 86$.
solutions.elegant: Half the perimeter, $43$ feet, is one width plus one length. Taking away the extra $7$ feet leaves $36$, which is two equal widths, so $w = 18$.

author: Devansh Sanghavi
